April 2011, Düsseldorf.jpg|thumb|The [[Hyundai i10]] (discontinued-2016) was exclusively manufactured by HMIL.]] '''Hyundai Motor India Limited (HMIL)''' is the Indian subsidiary of the South Korean automobile manufacturer [[Hyundai Motor Company]]. It is the second largest car manufacturer in India by sales until 2025.{{cite news |title=IPO-bound Hyundai India and its rivals in the world's third-biggest car market |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/ipo-bound-hyundai-india-its-rivals-worlds-third-biggest-car-market-2024-06-15/ |access-date=4 October 2024 |work=Reuters}} ==History== Hyundai Motor India Limited was formed on 6 May 1996 by the [[Hyundai Motor Company]] of [[South Korea]]. When Hyundai Motor Company entered the [[Automotive industry in India|Indian automobile market]] in 1996 the Hyundai brand was almost unknown throughout India. During the entry of Hyundai in 1996, there were only five major automobile manufacturers in India, i.e. [[Maruti Udyog Limited|Maruti]], [[Hindustan Motors|Hindustan]], [[Premier Automobiles Limited|Premier]], [[TATA Motors|Tata]] and [[Mahindra & Mahindra Limited|Mahindra]]. [[Daewoo Motors|Daewoo]] had entered the Indian automobile market with [[Daewoo Cielo#1994.E2.80.931997: Daewoo Cielo|Cielo]] just three years back while [[Ford India Private Limited|Ford]], [[Opel]] and [[Honda Siel Cars India|Honda]] had entered less than a year back.{{Citation needed|date=February 2023}} For more than a decade till Hyundai arrived, [[Maruti Suzuki]] had a near [[monopoly]] over the passenger cars segment because [[Tata Motors]] and [[Mahindra & Mahindra]] were solely utility and commercial vehicle manufacturers, while Hindustan and Premier both built outdated and uncompetitive products.{{Citation needed|date=February 2023}} HMIL's first car, the [[Hyundai Santro]] was launched on 23 September 1998 and was a runaway success. Within a few months of its inception, HMIL became India's second-largest automobile manufacturer and the largest automobile exporter. Hyundai Motor India Limited (HMIL) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Company (HMC), South Korea and is the second largest passenger car exporter and the second largest car manufacturer in India.{{Cite news |last=Mukherjee |first=Sharmistha |date=2025-04-02 |title=India's car exports hit record in FY25, Maruti leads the way |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/auto-news/indias-car-exports-hit-record-in-fy25-maruti-leads-the-way/articleshow/119880611.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-05-17 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} Hyundai started the construction of the plant in the year 1996. December 10, 1996 the groundbreaking ceremony was done for Plant 1. Mr Yang Soo Kim was then the managing director of Hyundai Motor India.{{Citation needed|date=February 2023}} The Indian counterpart leadership team was managed by Mr AP Gandhi, Mr BVR Subbu and Mr G.S. Ramesh. Mr AP Gandhi was the president for a few years of inception. Mr BVR Subbu was the marketing director responsible for dealer development and sales. He resigned from Hyundai Motor India in 2006.{{cite web|url=http://in.rediff.com/money/2006/mar/24hyund.htm |title=B V R Subbu quits Hyundai }} HMC has set up a research and development facility (Hyundai Motor India Engineering – HMIE) in the cyber city of Hyderabad. As HMC's global export hub for compact cars, HMIL became the first automotive company in India to achieve the export of 10 lakh cars in just over a decade. HMIL currently exports cars to more than 87 countries.{{cite web|url=http://motorbash.com/eight-years-counting-hyundai-india-is-the-top-exporter-of-the-year/|title=Eight Years & Counting, Hyundai India is the 'Top Exporter' of the Year|date=26 September 2013|publisher=motorbash.com}} In July 2012, [[Arvind Saxena]], the Director of Marketing and Sales stepped down from the position after serving the company for seven years.{{Cite web |title=Arvind Saxena resigns from Hyundai |url=https://www.zigwheels.com/news-features/news/arvind-saxena-resigns-from-hyundai/13677/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |website=ZigWheels.com |language=en}} In August 2018, Rakesh Srivastava, Director of Sales and Marketing at Hyundai India, resigned from his position after serving for six years. On 4 December 2018, Hyundai Motor India Ltd, announced the top-level management changes immediately. Seon Seob Kim assumed the responsibilities of MD and CEO from Young Key Koo.{{citation needed|date=April 2020}} In 2019, Hyundai Motor Company invested around 1.1 trillion KRW in an additional EV production line and began manufacturing Kona Electric. In 2022, Hyundai Motor India Limited receives about 85% of its electrical power as eco-friendly energy from external power plants. Moreover, it is currently installing a stationary solar power system of 1.9MWp using the module factory's roof with a size of 13,028m². On 15 June 2024, Hyundai Motor India filed a draft prospectus with the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] seeking approval for an initial public offering.{{cite web |author1=Sethuraman N R |author2=Nandan Mandayam |author3=Aditi Shah |title=Hyundai deepens India bet, files for IPO that could be country's biggest |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/hyundai-unit-files-ipo-india-2024-06-15/ |website=Reuters |access-date=19 June 2024 |date=15 June 2024}} [[File:HyundaiChennai.JPG|thumb|Hyundai's manufacturing plant near [[Chennai]].|left]] [[File:Hyundai Cars at the port.jpg|thumb|Hyundai Cars at a port.|left]] ==Manufacturing facilities== HMIL has two manufacturing plants, one in [[Irungattukottai]], [[Tamil Nadu]] and Other in [[Talegaon]], [[Maharashtra]]. [[Irungattukottai]] Plant has a capacity of 850,000 vehicles per annum.{{Cite web |last=Dutta |first=Aritro |title=Hyundai Motors Manufacturing Facilities in India |url=https://motomotar.com/hyundai/hyundai-motors-manufacturing-facilities-in-india/ |website=MotoMotar |date=2024-07-23 |access-date=2026-02-16}} ==R&D centre== Hyundai Motor India Engineering (HMIE) is a fully owned subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Company, South Korea, which is located at Hyderabad, Telangana. HMIL established HMIE in November 2006 and contributed to the development of Hyundai Motors' popular new models for the Indian market starting with the Eon and followed now by the "i" series, and also in SUV segments like the Creta. Hyundai Motors' other overseas R&D centres are located in the United States, Germany, Japan, Korea, and China.{{Citation needed|date=February 2023}} ==Global Quality Centre== {{unreferenced section|date=April 2020}} Indian Quality Centre (INQC) is one of five quality centres worldwide, along with those in the US, China, Europe and Middle East.{{Cite news |date=2017-04-28 |title=Hyundai opens quality centre in India to develope new cars and quality improvement |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/hyundai-opens-quality-centre-in-india-to-develope-new-cars-and-quality-improvement/articleshow/58414663.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-06-15 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} The India centre located at Faridabad, Haryana will conduct durability studies of existing models and benchmark parts and systems for constant improvement. The key activity of the centre is to "contribute in new car development from pilot stage to create quality product with zero defect". The centre will also be responsible for ensuring "top level safety quality" through proactive customer oriented management system and understanding feedback from them to eliminate potential risks. The centre also has an objective to study market conditions and other Asia Pacific regions to develop new cars and adapt strategies for continuous product quality improvement. The company opened a training centre at the facility. It will have its own body and paint unit. HMIL has the second largest sales and service network in India after [[Maruti Suzuki]].{{cite web|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/management/hyundai-s-price-jolt-for-maruti-114031201116_1.html|title=Hyundai's price jolt for Maruti|first=Sharmistha|last=Mukherjee|date=12 March 2014|via=Business Standard}} == Sales and exports == {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin:1em auto; font-size:97%; text-align:right;" |+Hyundai Motor India Limited annual sales |- !Year||Domestic sales||Exports||Total |- |1998||8,447||0||8,447 |- |1999||17,627||20||17,647 |- |2000||82,896||3,823||86,719 |- |2001||87,175||6,092||93,267 |- |2002||102,806||8,245||111,051 |- |2003||120,325||30,416||150,741 |- |2004||139,759||75,871||215,630 |- |2005||156,291||96,560||252,851 |- |2006||186,174||113,339||299,513 |- |2007||200,411||126,749||327,160 |- |2008||245,397||243,919||489,316 |- |2009||289,863||270,017||559,880 |- |2010||356,717||247,102||603,819 |- |2011||373,709||242,330||616,039 |- |2012||391,276||250,005||641,281 |- |2013||380,000||233,260||613,260 |- |2014||410,000||191,221||601,221 |- |2015||476,001||167,268||643,269 |- |2016||500,537||161,517||662,054 |- |2017||527,320||150,901||678,221 |- |2018||550,002||160,010||710,012 |- |2019||510,260||181,200||691,460
|} HMIL currently exports vehicles to over 92 countries across [[Africa]], [[Middle East]], [[Latin America]], [[Australia]] and [[Asia]]. In February 2010 HMIL achieved a record export of 1 million units.{{cite web|url=http://www.hyundai.com/in/en/AboutUs/HyundaiMotorIndia/WhoWeAre/index.html|title=Who We Are – HYUNDAI MOTOR INDIA – NEW THINKING. NEW POSSIBILITIES.|website=www.hyundai.com}} HMIL has been consecutively awarded "Top Exporter Of The Year" for 10 years by EEPC. The highest exported volume was 2,70,017 in year 2009. As of 2025, HMIL is the second largest car exporter in India following [[Maruti Suzuki]]. ==Awards and achievements== *'''Indian Car of the Year (ICOTY)'''{{citation needed|date=July 2021}} **2008 — Hyundai i10 **2014 — Hyundai Grand i10 **2015 — Hyundai Elite i20 **2016 — Hyundai Creta **2018 — Hyundai Verna **2020 — Hyundai Venue **2021 - Hyundai i20 *J D Power Appeal Awards 2016 demonstrating excellence of 'Made In India' Products as per global standards for Grand i10, Elite i20 & Creta.{{citation needed|date=July 2021}} *JD Power Indian Customer Satisfaction Award 2017 – For Ranking Number 1 in After Sales Customer satisfaction.{{citation needed|date=July 2021}} ==Brand ambassador== The carmaker got [[Shah Rukh Khan]] on board as its brand ambassador for the Hyundai Xcent, the company's recently launched sub-compact sedan in India. 1998, SRK shot his first TVC for the Hyundai Santro, and his association with the car brand has now turned 23.{{citation needed|date=July 2021}} In 2010 Khan won the "Brand Ambassador of the Year" for Hyundai i10 at NDTV Profit Car and Bike Awards.{{citation needed|date=July 2021}} Khan also promotes the "Be The Better Guy" road safety campaign for Hyundai.{{citation needed|date=July 2021}} In July 2017, Hyundai India extended Khan's contract for two years.{{cite web|title=Shah Rukh Khan as brand ambassador for Hyundai Xcent in India |url=http://carandme.com/media/news/shah-rukh-khan-to-be-new-brand-ambassador-for-hyundai/ |publisher=CarAndMe.com |access-date=23 September 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622132422/http://carandme.com/media/news/shah-rukh-khan-to-be-new-brand-ambassador-for-hyundai/ |archive-date=22 June 2015 }}{{cite web|title=Shah Rukh Khan as brand ambassador for Hyundai Xcent in India | url=http://www.zigwheels.com/news-features/news/shah-rukh-khan-roped-in-as-brand-ambassador-for-hyundai-xcent/19766/|publisher=ZigWheels.com|access-date=23 September 2013}} In 2024 Hyundai Motor India appointed [[Deepika Padukone]] as brand ambassador along with [[Shah Rukh Khan]] ahead with Hyundai Creta Facelift. ==Charging Network== Hyundai Motor India has added 11 ultra-fast charging stations strategically located across major highways and cities in India. And have plans to install 100 more charging stations by 2027.{{Cite web |url= https://motorlane.in/special-reviews/hyundai-motor-india-added-11-new-high-speed-ev-charging-network-across-india-100-more-by-2027 | title = Hyundai Motor India Added 11 New High-Speed EV Charging Network Across India. 100 More by 2027 | publisher=Motorlane| date= February 18, 2024}} == Hyundai Motor India Foundation == In 2021, the Hyundai Motor India Foundation (HMIF), the philanthropic arm of Hyundai Motor India Ltd., announced a new initiative, Art for Hope. It will work towards encouraging artists across various domains like digital arts, crafts, multidisciplinary arts, performance arts and visual arts. The project is scheduled to begin October 2021. Selected artists will get an opportunity to exchange ideas, complete an art project and be mentored by key industry people. The final projects will be displayed in art shows across India.{{Cite web|title=Hyundai's 'Art for Hope' to aid artists|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/chennai/2021/sep/28/hyundaisart-for-hope-to-aid-artists-2364529.html|access-date=2021-09-30|website=The New Indian Express}} ==See also== * [[Hyundai Motor Group]] * [[Automotive industry in India]] * [[List of Hyundai Motor Company manufacturing facilities]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category}} * [https://www.hyundai.com/in/en Hyundai Motor India Limited Official Website] {{Hyundai Motor Company}} {{Korean automobile industry}} {{Automotive industry in India}} [[Category:Hyundai Motor Company|India]] [[Category:Car manufacturers of India]] [[Category:Motor vehicle manufacturers based in Chennai]] [[Category:Vehicle manufacturing companies established in 1996]] [[Category:Indian subsidiaries of foreign companies]] [[Category:manufacturing companies based in Gurgaon]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1996]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]] [[Category:2024 initial public offerings]]
